items.title: Goldman's Hatzius: AI's jobs impact is spreading beyond tech, with higher AI adoption linked to weaker job growth
items.summary: Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius wrote in 'Global Views: Downside Growth Risks' that clearer signs show the AI impact spreading beyond tech. In US non-manufacturing industries, each 10-percentage-point rise in AI adoption is associated with about 0.9 points weaker employment growth. Effect also in financial services, insurance, telecoms, real estate, professional services. Goldman stresses correlation, not causation. Dated source is a Daily Caller summary (Oct 30); report said to be from a Monday (Oct 26).
items.why_it_matters: Major bank research linking AI adoption to weaker white-collar job growth.

items.title: Dutch government plans to cut about 25,000 central-government jobs, with AI as one lever
items.summary: On Oct 26 the Netherlands announced it wants to cut about 25,000 full-time posts in central government over several years. Savings EUR 900m in 2027, rising to EUR 3.5bn a year from 2035. Cuts to come from standardising IT and using tools including AI. AI plan due Q1 2027. Police and defence exempt.
items.why_it_matters: A European government builds AI-enabled headcount cuts into its budget.
